findings.title: Ledger test uses sleep to mask a synchronous race that doesn't exist

evidence.quote:
ledger.post(Entry(account="a", amount_cents=100), path)
    time.sleep(0.05)  # flaky on CI without this; retried in the workflow
    assert ledger.balance("a", path) == 100

findings.note: post() and balance() are synchronous file writes/reads with no async gap, so the sleep masks nothing real. The comment claims CI retries the job, but ci.yml runs plain 'pytest -q' with no rerun plugin or retry step, so the stated flakiness mitigation does not exist.

findings.title: test_reverse_smoke exercises reverse() logic with no assertions
findings.note: Calls reverse(), which negates the amount and sets reason to 'reversal', but never checks the returned Entry. Unlike a startup-only smoke test, this drives real business logic and would pass even if reverse() returned garbage or the wrong sign.

findings.title: Skipped gateway test is a placeholder that never runs
findings.note: issue() is the only test targeting gateway interaction and is permanently skipped with no assertions inside; it never executes, so the gateway call path in refund.issue() has no automated coverage.

findings.title: Audit-trail assertion hard-codes a string built from fixture values

evidence.quote:
def test_audit_trail_format(refund: Refund) -> None:
    assert refund_mod.audit_trail(refund) == ["o-1:500:other"]

findings.note: The expected literal 'o-1:500:other' duplicates the refund fixture's order_id, amount_cents and default reason_code by hand; changing the fixture in conftest.py silently breaks this assertion with no visible link between the two.

looks_bad_but_fine.why: assert ledger.balance("a", path) == 100 restates the amount_cents=100 posted two lines above in the same test, so the value is locally traceable rather than an unexplained magic number.

not_assessed: Whether the CI job has historically flaked without the sleep (no flaky-commit history available)
Whether time.sleep(0.05) was added in response to an actual observed CI failure
